event.summary: Report-discard contract does not match gone host terminals
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f96dd4363d97dc7e07dea5b8947c96be6bf912e8

## TLDR
The implementation specification now says pending conversation reports are discarded when their terminal no longer exists. Terminal hosts instead retain the launch anchor after disappearing, allowing a valid report to be admitted; if the session has no terminal object, the report is retried. Someone maintaining this logic from the new specification could incorrectly discard a final conversation report and leave Restart pointing at older state. The reviewed change is a documentation error; no current runtime regression or observed loss of conversation is claimed.

## Details
SPEC_impl.md:4643–4644 replaces the old missing-pane statement with: 'A report made under an earlier launch, or whose terminal no longer exists, fails the anchor and is discarded.' That substitution does not describe the host replacement. At this commit, crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/hosts/terminal.rs:864–881 deliberately keeps the child pid/start anchor for Liveness::Gone as well as Running and Exited; its documentation explicitly says the anchor is kept after exit so a report written before exit may still be applied. HostTerminal::anchor at :2548–2550 exposes that retained anchor. service/core.rs:15776–15802 obtains the current-generation host anchor, returning Internal if there is no terminal object or no readable anchor. service/report_files.rs:320–324 passes an available anchor to procs::anchor_chain; procs.rs:547–580 checks the report's recorded pid/start and chain integrity without requiring the terminal to be alive. A valid final report can therefore pass after the host is gone. With no terminal object, report_files.rs:247–265 instead maps Internal to Disposition::Retry. These are two distinct counterexamples to the new discard wording, established through source rather than execution.

Fix the text to distinguish an ancestry mismatch from a vanished terminal, describe the retained post-exit anchor, and describe missing/unreadable current-generation host state as retryable. The source locations above establish the contract without reproducing a bug. Revision of l2: investigation settled the lead; the drain has no extra terminal-gone discard condition.

Suggested bucket: other, for an inaccurate internal contract. Confidence: confirmed by source analysis. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none (coverage sources not searched). Could-be-highest: no established shipped security or loss-of-work route; the possible future implementation mistake is motivation for correcting the documentation, not a claim of current highest impact. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: Automatic-tab cleanup contract omits failed-close retries
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f96dd4363d97dc7e07dea5b8947c96be6bf912e8

## TLDR
The rewritten implementation contract says automatic tab cleanup proceeds only when the runtime reports that the shell exited. It also retries previously authorized closes whose host could not be confirmed ended, even when the aborted runtime still reports running or unavailable. Following the new absolute condition would suppress that recovery and could leave failed tab closes unfinished. This is a documentation contradiction; no current runtime cleanup failure is claimed.

## Details
Assigned changed text at SPEC_impl.md:4826–4827 says 'Automatic tab cleanup goes ahead only while the tab’s runtime says its shell exited, checked under its lifecycle claim before signalling'. The parent hunk instead described rechecking a tmux window; this commit introduces the absolute host-runtime-exit statement. git log -S over the full exclusive 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a through inclusive 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db range attributes that new phrase to this commit. The runtime files are unchanged by this documentation commit. Its only later in-range SPEC_impl.md diff changes unrelated setup wording, not this assertion.

At the reviewed revision, service/core/host_tabs.rs:146–156 explains that a failed host end aborts the runtime, leaving its old status possibly running forever, so automatic reaping must retry it. :193–199 explicitly checks end_failed/retry_at before finished(); :312–332 marks and schedules those retries. service/ticker.rs:1651–1662 consumes that due list and calls try_close_tab. service/core.rs:13923–13935 takes the lifecycle claim and passes only_if_dead=true through close_tab_claimed; :13989–14012 resolves the same tab and invokes its host close. No caller adds a fresh shell-exit requirement. Back in host_tabs.rs:929–932, end_failed bypasses the unavailable-runtime refusal, and :963–969 checks reap_due again under the claim. The failure path at :1025–1028 marks the tab for precisely this later retry. These checks establish an automatic cleanup path without the specified runtime-exit observation. Independently, finished at :181–185 also admits a gone host, which need not have delivered a shell-exit record.

The complete Tabs in hosts contract at SPEC_impl.md:2262–2264 correctly describes the exception: 'A close that cannot confirm the end keeps the tab and its record and marks it, and since its stopped runtime announces nothing, the reap closes it again until one does'. That accurate rule and the working runtime do not reconcile the later absolute only-while-exited condition. Qualify :4826 to cover ordinary first-time dead-tab reap plus continuation of a previously authorized failed close. The retry is finishing that earlier close; this finding does not allege it obtains new authority to stop unrelated live work.
